result.title: Rethinking Asymmetry in Self-Supervised 3D Geometry Learning
result.summary: Self-supervised learning relies on asymmetry between what a model observes and what it must explain. Recent methods learn 3D geometry from unposed images by predicting cameras and scene structure, then rendering held-out views. To avoid trivial solutions, they impose this asymmetry in the input space, restricting how views interact through separate branches or masked attention. We revisit this design with geometric accuracy, rather than rendering quality, as the main objective. When a held-out view lies between context views, the context already constrains the geometry it observes. We therefore impose the asymmetry in the 3D representation space, excluding held-out views only from the reconstructed scene while a shared backbone uses all views for correspondence. This improves depth and pose estimation over input-space designs. We further exploit view density: sparse and dense observations depict the same scene but provide different amounts of correspondence. Aligning sparse-context features with dense-context features supplies a geometric training signal alongside rendering, without a pretrained geometric teacher. We additionally align features with a frozen vision foundation model, which brings further gains. None of these signals requires geometric annotation, and the resulting model improves geometry estimation over prior self-supervised methods. Controlled experiments isolate the contribution of each component, and self-supervised pretraining also improves subsequent supervised training.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以几何精度而非渲染质量为目标，重新审视无位姿图像的自监督 3D 学习：把非对称约束从输入空间移到 3D 表示空间，让共享骨干利用全部视角做对应、仅在重建场景中排除留出视角，并用稀疏/密集上下文特征对齐及冻结视觉基础模型特征对齐作为额外训练信号。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「表示空间施加不对称」与「稀疏—密集特征对齐提供无教师监督」的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中如何用内部表示对齐作为训练信号、以及几何信息是否真正保留在 latent 状态中；但论文面向 3D 重建，与 VLM 推理的联系需较多核查。
